Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Hypersensitivity to acetazolamide or any excipients in the formulation.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Since acetazolamide is a sulfonamide derivative, cross sensitivity between acetazolamide, sulfonamides and other sulfonamide derivatives is possible.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Acetazolamide therapy is contraindicated in situations in which sodium and/or potassium blood serum levels are depressed, in cases of marked kidney and liver disease or dysfunction, in suprarenal gland failure, and in hyperchloremic acidosis.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: It is contraindicated in patients with cirrhosis because of the risk of development of hepatic encephalopathy.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: The safety and effectiveness of acetazolamide extended-release capsules in pediatric patients below the age of 12 years have not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Metabolic acidosis, which can be severe, may occur in the elderly with reduced renal function.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Teratogenic effects Acetazolamide, administered orally or parenterally, has been shown to be teratogenic (defects of the limbs) in mice, rats, hamsters, and rabbits.

sourceReadings.label: Acetazolamide label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants from acetazolamide, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or to discontinue the drug taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.

sourceReadings.excerpt: WARNING Increased Mortality in Elderly Patients with Dementia-Related Psychosis Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death.

sourceReadings.label: Prochlorperazine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Do not use in comatose states or in the presence of large amounts of central nervous system depressants (alcohol, barbiturates, narcotics, etc.).

sourceReadings.excerpt: Do not use in pediatric patients under 2 years of age or under 20 lbs.

sourceReadings.label: Prochlorperazine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Do not use in children for conditions for which dosage has not been established.

sourceReadings.label: Prochlorperazine label

sourceReadings.label: Prochlorperazine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: NON-TERATOGENIC EFFECTS Neonates exposed to antipsychotic drugs, during the third trimester of pregnancy are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms following delivery.

sourceReadings.label: Prochlorperazine label
sourceReadings.excerpt: There is evidence that phenothiazines are excreted in the breast milk of nursing mothers.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Patients with a history of hypertriglyceridemia-induced pancreatitis ( 4 )

sourceReadings.excerpt: Regulation of glucose metabolism is the primary activity of insulins and insulin analogs, including insulin lispro.

sourceReadings.label: Insulin Lispro Recombinant label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Insulins lower blood glucose by stimulating peripheral glucose uptake by skeletal muscle and fat, and by inhibiting hepatic glucose production.

sourceReadings.label: Insulin Lispro Recombinant label

sourceReadings.label: Methylnaltrexone label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Methylnaltrexone is a selective antagonist of opioid binding at the mu-opioid receptor.

sourceReadings.label: Methylnaltrexone label
sourceReadings.excerpt: As a quaternary amine, the ability of methylnaltrexone to cross the blood-brain barrier is restricted.

sourceReadings.label: Methylnaltrexone label
sourceReadings.excerpt: This allows methylnaltrexone to function as a peripherally-acting mu-opioid receptor antagonist in tissues such as the gastrointestinal tract, thereby decreasing the constipating effects of opioids without impacting opioid-mediated analgesic effects on the central nervous system (CNS).

sourceReadings.excerpt: CTLA-4 is a negative regulator of T-cell activity.

sourceReadings.label: Ipilimumab label

sourceReadings.excerpt: Ranibizumab products bind to the receptor binding site of active forms of VEGF-A, including the biologically active, cleaved form of this molecule, VEGF 110 .

sourceReadings.label: Ranibizumab-Eqrn label

sourceReadings.excerpt: Rucaparib is an inhibitor of poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) enzymes, including PARP-1, PARP-2, and PARP-3, which play a role in DNA repair.

sourceReadings.label: Rucaparib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: In vitro studies have shown that rucaparib-induced cytotoxicity may involve inhibition of PARP enzymatic activity and increased formation of PARP-DNA complexes resulting in DNA damage, apoptosis, and cancer cell death.

sourceReadings.label: Rucaparib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Increased rucaparib-induced cytotoxicity and anti-tumor activity was observed in tumor cell lines with deficiencies in BRCA1/2 and other DNA repair genes.

sourceReadings.label: Rucaparib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Rucaparib has been shown to decrease tumor growth in mouse xenograft models of human cancer with or without deficiencies in BRCA .

Sebetralstat label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Sebetralstat is a competitive, reversible inhibitor of plasma kallikrein.

sourceReadings.label: Sebetralstat label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Plasma kallikrein is a serine protease that cleaves high molecular weight kininogen (HK) releasing bradykinin which increases vascular permeability through activation of bradykinin receptors causing edema.

sourceReadings.label: Sebetralstat label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Sebetralstat inhibits the cleavage of HK and reduces production of bradykinin, thereby treating the clinical symptoms of an acute, episodic attack of HAE.

sourceReadings.label: Sebetralstat label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Sebetralstat also inhibits the positive feedback mechanism of the kallikrein kinin system by plasma kallikrein, thereby reducing factor XIIa and additional plasma kallikrein generation.

Upadacitinib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upadacitinib is a Janus kinase (JAK) inhibitor.

sourceReadings.label: Upadacitinib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: JAKs are intracellular enzymes which transmit signals arising from cytokine or growth factor-receptor interactions on the cellular membrane to influence cellular processes of hematopoiesis and immune cell function.

sourceReadings.label: Upadacitinib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Within the signaling pathway, JAKs phosphorylate and activate signal transducers and activators of transcription (STATs) which modulate intracellular activity including gene expression.

sourceReadings.label: Upadacitinib label
sourceReadings.excerpt: Upadacitinib modulates the signaling pathway at the point of JAKs, preventing the phosphorylation and activation of STATs.

sourceReadings.excerpt: Gaucher disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the GBA gene, which results in a deficiency of the lysosomal enzyme beta-glucocerebrosidase.

caveats: A density score describes a record in this corpus. It does not describe a medicine, and it does not describe the published evidence about a medicine. A low score means the corpus holds little here, and nothing more than that.
A record with no entry in a module is a record where nobody has yet structured that module from a source. Absence here is neither a favourable nor an unfavourable finding about the medicine.
The weighting is a stated convention chosen for this index, not a measured quantity. Each component is published beside the score so a different weighting can be applied to the same components.

Two documents count as one when they share a source kind and identifier. A document that was revised between two fetch dates therefore still counts once, so corroboration may be reported slightly higher than it is.
The retrieval dates are the dates source artifacts were fetched during authoring. They say when the corpus last looked, not when the source last changed.

The coverage queue was designed to rank widely marketed medicines first, using the count of recorded product variants as the proxy. This corpus cannot express that: the largest number of product variants on any record is 2, and the largest number of distinct jurisdictions on any record is 1, so the module reports little more than whether a marketed product entry was recorded at all. The queue is instead ordered by how much already-cited source material a record has left unstructured, and it does not rank medicines by prominence.
The queue cutoff is the median density of 0.555 among records holding a marketed product entry, chosen and stated in advance rather than tuned against the length of queue it produces.

Records assembled by the deterministic label parser and records assembled by a person are measured on the same scale here. The scale does not distinguish the two kinds of work; the provenance tier on each value does.
Values recorded as displayed text with no parsed number are counted separately rather than penalised as missing. A source that prints no number is recorded faithfully when no number is stored.
